page: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with an x86_64 architecture, this server features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with a massive memory allocation of 1792.0 GB, translating to 28.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Additionally, the instance includes 7340 GB of local storage, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is consistently categorized in the bottom 10%, as evidenced by poor scores in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression tests. However, the server leverages its high core count to achieve average multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads and writes, perform in the middle 50% tier. Large-scale operations such as Redis SET and Passmark database benchmarks also demonstrate average performance.

Given its hardware profile, the M64m is designed for memory-heavy workloads that require substantial RAM capacity and local storage rather than high single-threaded compute speeds. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is centered on its high resource density, offering a massive memory-to-vCPU ratio that reduces the need to scale out to multiple nodes for large in-memory datasets. It is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise resource planning applications, and data warehousing. However, it is poorly suited for tasks requiring rapid single-threaded execution or intensive LLM text generation, where it exhibits weak to poor performance.
description: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a 2.7 GHz clock speed. It features an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1792.0 GB (28.0 GB per core) and 7340 GB of local storage, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmark evaluations indicate a significant tradeoff: single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations achieve average tier results. Lacking GPU acceleration, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory density rather than raw single-threaded compute power. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications.
